title: Fake Merc Character Study (part. 4): Casting Couch
summary: Fourth part of NH's mocking drama series about a powerlifting YouTuber he calls the fake mercenary, attacking his health, posture, physique, coaching claims, honesty and 'just trolling' excuses. Training takeaways are scattered: push-up baselines, posture and mobility, pull-ups and shoulder health, and what a coach should be.
claims: Years hunched at a computer cause forward head posture and a hunchback that destroy mobility, limiting squat depth and many lifts
Pull-ups and chin-ups are excellent for the shoulders; they become dangerous only with poor shoulder mobility
Once past basic muscular development, an adult male should never drop below 20 push-ups; he can still do 20 after two hours of benching
A distorted mass-to-strength ratio robs you of moving your body through space; immobile powerlifters at least trade dynamic for static strength
Over-focusing on squats and deadlifts while neglecting upper body work worsens a wide-waisted, narrow frame
Almost anyone can achieve a good physique with dedication and by listening to people who know what they are doing
A real coach is excited by talented prospects; resenting athletes with better potential disqualifies you as a coach
He started his channel during the COVID-19 lockdown and grew it on his own
About $200-250 a month is the top end for coaching; that buys an excellent powerlifting coach
Hiding behind 'I was just trolling' when caught is weak; admit you were wrong and move on
He does not ban commenters because, having trolled plenty online himself, he sees trolling he receives as karma
